translations.text: A lie.
Those who have inherited the kingdom of God forever.
Especially because they are impure, effeminate men, men who sleep with males, and anyone who defiles themselves in any way,
whether male or female, in all their congregations that exist within our way of life.
here, and everyone who practices any kind of deceit before God, secretly or openly.
If you do not see yourselves being like Satan in the blazing furnace of fire,
being punished together in Hades,
then all your deeds and all your plans are true,
and the words of the one who says these things are lies.
By the same author.
Therefore, let us not refuse to bear with one another, lest God become angry with us. For we have not yet spent long bearing with one another, like
the Lord and his Christ and his holy angels, who have borne with us from the beginning of creation until today, and will do so forever.
But let us serve one another like Jesus, who took the form of a servant for our sake.
And like Paul, the servant of Jesus.
And like all the apostles and all the prophets, who became servants of the Lord and his Christ, Jesus.
As the Scriptures say, “I sent you my servants, the prophets, day after day, early in the morning, and I sent them, but you did not listen.”
Did the prophets and the apostles serve the Lord or his Christ in [?], so that two would agree to suffer with others and die for the name of Jesus?

Therefore, when the Lord Jesus knew beforehand that the fathers, the apostles, would do everything he had commanded them, as he was about to leave them and go up to heaven according to the Scriptures,
and just as they also fulfilled what he had commanded them from the beginning, while the Lord of glory, Jesus, was with them,
therefore he said to them, “I will no longer call you my servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing.
Instead, I will call you my brothers and my friends, because I have told you everything I heard from my Father.
It was not you,” he said, “who chose me,
but I chose you.
And I am sending you like sheep among wolves.
Do not be afraid of those who will kill your body.
If they persecuted me, they will persecute you.
If they kept my word, they will keep yours too.
If they called [?]
Letter of Shenoute.
Abraham our father wanted to have children by Sarah.
And Sarah wanted to have children by Abraham.
And this is how the Lord God gave Abraham a son in his old age.
He fathered Isaac through Sarah in her old age.
He became a beloved son to them, like ten thousand sons, though he was only one.
[?] is [?], [?] after his [?].
He came from his own body.
He also brought comfort to the mother who bore him.
And in this way he inherited his parents’ inheritance,
according to what was said to Abraham by God:
“That one, who is Ishmael, will not be your heir.
Nevertheless, I will also bless him for your sake,
and I will make him increase greatly,
and make him a great and numerous nation.
But the one who comes from your [?]—
Isaac [?] is the one who will be your heir.”
For this reason, she spoke boldly, with knowledge of God—
the mother of the son who was her own—
saying, “Throw out this slave woman and her son.
For the son of this slave woman will not inherit along with my son Isaac.”
Isaac was praying to the Lord, wanting to have children by Rebekah.
And Rebekah wanted to have children by Isaac.
And this is how the Lord God gave them what their hearts desired,
fulfilling all their requests.
They had Esau and Jacob.
And Isaac blessed Jacob through God, following the advice of Rebekah, Jacob’s mother.
Esau became Jacob’s slave, according to the Scriptures:
“The older will serve the younger.”
And again: “I loved Jacob, but I hated Esau.”
Jacob wanted to have children by Rachel,
like those he had by Leah,
and those he had by Zilpah and Bilhah.
Rachel wanted to have children by Jacob,
and she was distressed,
finding fault with Jacob in her ignorance,
in the intensity of her sorrow,
saying, “Give me children; otherwise I will die.”
And Jacob would say to her indignantly,
“Am I the Lord, I [?] withhold [?] fruit [?]?”
And Jacob said this falsely, because he too wanted to have children by Rachel.
And in this way God saw their distress,
and gave Jacob children by Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
And Jacob blessed all his children through the Lord God,
who blessed Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the children.
Therefore it is foolishness and blindness on our part,
If some among us initially refuse, with quarrelling and disobedience, tasks that they are able to attend to,
whether people entrusted to them, or acts of service, or any good work
that we can do for one another through God for the salvation of our souls.
And it is also an even greater folly and an evil hardness of heart
if some among you choose to be barren through God and stubbornly and ignorantly renounce tasks
that they are able to take care of, whether people, or acts of service, or any good work for you to do for one another in the fear of the Lord.
But if a woman living with a husband in the flesh is willing to have sons and daughters,
And if Sarah and Rebecca and Rachel and Hannah and the mother of the prophet Samson,
and Elizabeth, the mother of John, who was filled with the Holy Spirit while still in his mother’s womb,
if these and other holy women of ancient times cried out to the Lord, praying and pleading not to be barren,
then, if some among you abandon people who have been entrusted to them by God,
how disgraced they will be! For they have chosen for themselves to become barren and widowed,
For from the beginning until now, there have been many parents whom God has put to shame, whether men or women,
because they did not want to toil with others so that these might become their sons and daughters through God.
But because of bodily comfort and pride, many men have withdrawn so that they would not endure hardship with others through God,
as some others also endured hardship with them.
And many women have withdrawn so that they would not endure hardship with others through God,
as some others also endured hardship with them.
And because of their pride and their love of bodily comfort, they have chosen to remain barren,
and for the Lord to shut the doors of their soul as with a barren woman,
and to make the counsels of instruction dry up within us like withered breasts, so that from that time onward they no longer give milk by teaching others through God.
Yet there are also many parents, from the beginning until now, whom the Lord has blessed, whether male or female,
because they preferred to suffer with others through God.
like our ancient fathers, and the prophets and apostles, who became fathers of many multitudes through God,
And like Deborah, who became a judge and a mother in Israel, and like Huldah the prophetess,
whom the righteous King Josiah sent to consult, so that he might inquire of the Lord through her, and like Anna, the daughter of Phanuel,
“This is not the time for us to become parents of sons and daughters through God,” they say in their ignorance,
“for the Lord will give eunuchs and virgins a choice place and a name better than sons and daughters.”
And some among us here, or among you yourselves, choose this for themselves,
so that they may abandon those entrusted to them [?] and not take care of them, saying,
“We will please God,
and these people and those others are not our concern.”
And in their stubbornness they bring in the prophet’s words,
interpreting them according to their own hearts’ desires and their own comfort, saying,
“The Lord will give eunuchs and virgins a kingdom of heaven.”
And in this way they abandon others so that they do not have to take care of them.
[?] that [?] it.
[?] that they have never [?] learned from the apostle, who [?] says,
“Do not let [?] seek his own advantage, but that of another,
Just as he, too, did not seek his own benefit, but that of many.
so that they may be saved.”
Especially the prophet, whose words the ignorant interpret according to their own wishes:
“The Lord will give the [?] a place [?] chosen [?] and a name better than sons and daughters.”
Isaiah himself, too, not only endured many sufferings for the name of God,
but also died for great multitudes and for all of us.
A father or a mother who has sons and daughters, and their children's children, and many possessions,
and they are constrained by the affairs of life, never having the ability to [?] over [?]
sons and [?] daughters and [?] all the other affairs of this age.
and also care for sons and daughters through God, and all the other works of righteousness.
For people like these cannot serve those who belong to them according to the flesh
and also serve others through God.
But people who have no sons or daughters according to the flesh,
or, on the other hand, have them and renounce [?]
[?] according to what is fitting.
of the calling with which he called them into this life.
These are the eunuchs and the virgins—that is, you, brothers and sisters, and everyone who practices self-restraint everywhere
throughout the whole earth, whether those who do not know honorable marriage and the pure marriage bed, or those who have taken wives and those who have taken husbands,
and when they made their choice through God, following the counsel of the one who said,
not letting him repay those who kill them and flog them, as they drag them.
they throw them out beyond the city,
and everything they do to them in the synagogues and in the councils,
and how they bring them before governors and kings, and great sufferings extending even to death.
So, remembering the sufferings of all these saints,
and taking courage from the way our Lord Jesus disregarded the shame,
enduring the cross for the salvation of us all,
For he is our Savior; he is our Lord and our Father.
and also knowing this: that the good and compassionate God bears with all of us, from one end of the earth to the other end of the inhabited world,
from the beginning, when he created humanity on the earth, down to this very day,
and that he will continue to bear with us until the end of the age, in the abundance of his mercy,
because we are his servants, and he is our ruler and our king.
Therefore, let us not refuse to bear with one another, lest God become angry with us. For we have not yet spent long bearing with one another, like the Lord and his Christ
and his holy angels, who have borne with us from the beginning of creation until today, and will do so forever.
Instead, let us serve one another like Jesus, who took the form of a servant for our sake.
And like Paul, the servant of Jesus.
And like all the apostles and all the prophets, who became servants of the Lord and of his Christ, Jesus.
According to the Scriptures: “I sent you my servants, the prophets, early each day. I sent them, but you did not listen.”
In what way did the prophets and the apostles serve the Lord or his Christ, except by choosing to suffer with others and to die for the name of Jesus?
Therefore, since the Lord Jesus knew beforehand that our fathers the apostles would do everything he had commanded them,
as he was about to leave them and go up to heaven, according to the Scriptures,
and likewise, since they had fulfilled what he had commanded them from the beginning, while the Lord of glory, Jesus, was with them,
for this reason he said to them, “From now on, I will no longer call you my servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing.
Instead, I will call you my brothers and my friends, because I have told you everything I heard from my Father.
“It was not you,” he said, “who chose me.”
But I chose you.
And I am sending you like sheep among wolves.
Do not be afraid of those who will kill your body.
If they persecuted me, they will persecute you.
If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they harass the members of his household with mockery and contempt!”
See now, brothers, how far we fall short, for our fathers, the prophets and the apostles, endured great sufferings in strenuous service,
among the wicked and the good, and among those who hated them and those who loved them.
But we ourselves are not ashamed to say,
“We will not take care of our brothers,”
showing ourselves unworthy of the grace of the Lord, who made us worthy to draw near to him through deeds
of which we are not worthy.
For this reason, do not let anyone among us or among you yourselves squander the grace of the Lord
and flee from others to whom they have been assigned to provide care by God,
just as others also took care of them from the beginning.
and now, too, while others take care of them in every matter, whether in instruction in the Scriptures or in food
and clothing, and also in their sickness and in every matter in which those who care for them serve them,
For this reason, let us not lie by saying, “Those who govern us are our masters,
and we are beneath them like slaves.”
Those who rule over us are not above us.
Rather, we are above them, and they are beneath us.
Or they serve as our slaves, because they take care of us in every matter through God.
How did the prophets, the apostles, and all the saints, from the beginning until now, agree to become slaves to others so that they too might receive life?
Was it not because they saw the Lord of glory, Jesus, taking the form of a slave for our sake?
And again, from the beginning God became a worker like a slave, though he is the Lord and the King.
Just as he made his angels spirits, as it is written.
And just as he created everything out of what did not exist.
He brought them all into being—the heavens, the earth, and everything in them—according to the Scriptures.
“You laid the foundation of the earth.
The heavens are the works of your hands.”
And again, just as he spoke so that everything would come into being.
And they all came into being at his command:
the cattle, the sheep, all the other animals of the field, and all the birds of the sky,
and the creatures in the waters of the rivers, the trees that bear fruit, and everything that grows from the earth, according to the Scriptures.
And again, just as God took some earth from the ground, after consulting with Jesus, the firstborn of all creation,
who exists before them all, saying, “Let us make a human being in our image and according to our likeness.”
And when they had created the human being in their image and according to their likeness, according to the Scriptures,
God breathed a breath of life into his face.
The human being became a living soul.
God created them male and female, as it is written.
And just as God planted a garden in Eden, he placed there this human being [?]
and with you.
So that we may truly become children of Abraham and children of all our ancient fathers,
whom the Lord blessed.
For they loved not only their sons and daughters according to the flesh and all who belonged to them,
but they loved everyone who believes in God and keeps God's commandments.
And in this way their offspring inherited everyone who would be faithful and righteous,
from the beginning down to this very day, and forever.
But if disobedient and sinful children were born to our ancestors,
They did not reject their righteous children, causing them to flee from them,
because of the abundance of unruly behavior among the wicked children.
Instead, they cut off the sinful children from themselves.
They remained with their righteous children all the days of their lives.
Therefore, just as many sinful children grieved our fathers of old,
so also many righteous children made them glad.
And just as God often becomes angry enough to wipe out many peoples of old because of the many sinful children among them,
so also God often turns his wrath away from many peoples of old because of the righteous children who arose among them.
And just as great multitudes died in their wickedness, in every kind of lawlessness, because of many false prophets
who arose among many peoples of old, honoring them, misleading them, and bringing God's wrath down upon them and themselves,
so also great multitudes lived in every kind of righteousness because of many prophets of the Lord God
who arose among many peoples of old, speaking the truth
and rebuking those who sin, while declaring those who do good blessed.
And just as those who misled them came from the peoples of old—that is, the false prophets and the priests who mislead—
so also the prophets of the Lord God came from the peoples of old, namely:
Moses, Joshua the prophet, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel,
and all the prophets who rebuked everyone who sinned or would sin before the Lord,
and who encouraged everyone who practiced or would practice every kind of righteousness.
Now all the prophets of the Lord God and the apostles of our Lord Jesus
are all descended from the offspring of our father Abraham.
and they did not spare Abraham's descendants when they sinned before God, who created them,
But they brought great curses down upon their brothers who were descended from them.
according to everything written in the law of Moses.
And again, they blessed everyone who glorified the Lord God through their righteous deeds.
Still more, they cursed every false prophet, all the priests who lead people astray, and every antichrist.
And all the false teachers, and everyone who does not believe in our Lord Jesus, from the beginning until now.
But if all the prophets, all the apostles, all our fathers of old, and all the righteous, from the beginning to this day,
are people who practice the truth and speak the truth,
because the truth is within them,
and this is how they became upright in all their deeds through God,
then let us too, brothers, practice the truth and speak the truth, so that we may be upright in all our deeds,
and so that we may be counted among the prophets, the apostles, and all the saints,
and be worthy of God, because God is true.
And our Lord Jesus is true, he who said, “I am the truth.”
Therefore, let us not tell lies
about the evil deeds we do in darkness,
so that we will not be counted among those who belong to Satan,
in whom there is no truth,
because he is a liar,
and he has never stood in the truth.
That is why he is cursed, sowing lies and every sin among those who belong to him, as it is written:
“Whenever the liar speaks, he speaks from what is his own.” Understand, then, that everyone who commits sin and tells lies is counted among those who belong to
Satan.
Nor should we become traitors and thieves, so that we will not become like Judas, about whom he said through the Holy Spirit,
“Let the curse enter him like water, and like oil into his bones.”
Therefore, let us not be deceitful people before the Lord in any evil deed.
whether through impurity and defilement, or through theft and deceit, or through hatred and insolence, or through hypocrisy and empty glory.
Who are the insolent people, if not those who grumble
and shake their heads with great irritation and roll their eyes at those who guide them,
who care for them and teach them
to live in good order according to all God's ordinances.
Who are the hypocrites, if not people who have other people wrapped around them, covering up for those who commit transgression in every wicked deed?
Therefore, let us not go astray through falsehood and cover up one another’s sins,
for this is the downfall of every congregation that has sinned before God, from the beginning to this day.
Instead, let us teach one another not to sin before the Lord.
And again, if we go astray and commit a fault, let us rebuke one another.
For this is the strength and support of every congregation that has pleased the Lord from the beginning until now.
It is no wonder if we become like the false prophets and cover up one another’s sins,
and God pours his curse down upon us in anger and wrath.
But it is wonderful if we follow the example of our fathers, the prophets and the apostles,
and teach one another not to sin before God.
And again, even if we commit a fault through ignorance, let us rebuke one another so that we repent,
so that the Lord may pour his blessing down upon us in mercy and compassion.
Nevertheless, if it is right for us to say many things to you in this letter,
it is also right for us to be silent
and entrust you to God and all the words of the Scriptures, as the apostle says:
“I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which can build you up and give you the inheritance with all the saints.”
Now then, since you sent word to us
that the sister whom you appointed in place of the one who died has refused the work you assigned her,
we want you to tell us why she stopped carrying out the responsibility you assigned her,
so that, if we learn that she refused because she is unable to bear the work assigned to her, she may rest peacefully in the place where she lived before.
But if she refused out of stubbornness and lack of discipline,
then she herself will be found a liar before the Lord,
“I refused because I cannot do this.”
And after some days, or after some time, if we hear that she refused out of contentiousness, you will all know what you are to do to her.
because she did not tell us how she had been mistreated
or in what matter she had been oppressed.
And if we find that others are preventing her from telling the truth, we will deal with these others too, and they will not remain hidden from you,
because they and she have made a covenant with falsehood at Satan’s prompting.
After this, look, I have sent the elder to you,
so that you will remember God and have compassion for yourselves in your own community, and for us too in ours.
And tell us about all these errors among you.
For we have been afflicted with anguish, both we and you.
But people who have no sons or daughters according to the flesh,
or who do have them and renounce them,
along with many possessions, wishing to live in a way worthy of the calling
of the one who called them to this way of life—
these are the eunuchs and the virgins, namely you, brothers, and everyone who practices self-restraint everywhere throughout the whole earth,
whether those who do not know what honorable marriage and the undefiled marriage bed are, or those who have taken wives and those who have taken husbands, and then became willing,
through God, following the counsel of the one who said,
“Let whoever is able to bear it bear it.”
They renounced honorable marriage and the undefiled marriage bed,
and they renounced their sons and daughters, their brothers and their parents, and everything they owned,
remembering the Lord’s words:
“Whoever comes to me, hating his father and mother, his children, his brothers and sisters, and even his own life.”
People like these are the ones who will be able to become disciples of the Lord according to the Scriptures.
And these are the eunuchs who have no children according to the flesh,
but who have become fathers of many children of God.
For whether they have no children, or instead do have them but have renounced them all, along with everything they own,
they have taken up their cross and followed the Lord.
Our holy fathers, the prophets and the apostles, are people of this kind.
These truly are the ones who have become eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of God.
And this is how they have become fathers of many people, according to the Lord’s words:
“For everyone who has left a house, or a brother, or a sister, or a father, or a mother, or a wife, or a son, or a daughter,
or a field, for the sake of my name, will receive them many times over and inherit eternal life.”
Therefore, brothers, do not let each of us be a burden to his neighbor through the estrangement in our thinking that exists within us, as we are divided in our hearts toward one another.
For they compel us, through our thoughts of wisdom for ourselves [?] ourselves alone [?], not to care for one another.
Instead, as God’s fellow workers,
let each of us support his neighbor, whether great or small.
And let us love living with one another in peace,
without sin or deceit, like God and his angels who dwell [?] in heaven.
[?] wise children would not want to do the things their righteous father does?
What wise brothers would not follow the example of their faithful brothers who are greater than they are?
That is, what wise people would not want to do the deeds that their Father in heaven does,
that is, God and our Lord Jesus,
and follow the example of the Lord’s angels, the example of the prophets, and the example of Paul and all the apostles, who said
“Follow our conduct, our rule, our faith, our patience, our love, our endurance, our persecutions, and our sufferings.”
Then again: “We gave ourselves to you as an example.”
And again: “My brothers and sisters, take the prophets as an example of suffering and patience.”
again, “You shall make yourself an example in everything.”
Then again: “Likewise, the older men should conduct themselves in a holy manner.”
Above all, Scripture tells us about our Lord Jesus:
“He left you an example so that you might follow in his footsteps.”
What is the work of God and our Lord Jesus, if not the works [?] of his hands?
It is his hands that formed us and made us.
Therefore, according to the Scriptures, God and our Lord Jesus work for the salvation of every person right up to the present, according to the apostle’s words:
“The one who prepared us for this is God.”
What is the conduct of the angels in heaven,
if not to carry out their glorious works every day, blessing and glorifying God and our Lord Jesus,
and to perform services for those who live on earth, so that they may inherit salvation?
What is the conduct of the prophets and apostles, if not to choose for themselves to suffer with others, even to the point of death?
And in all these things they give thanks to the Lord, blessing those who curse them and praying for those who persecute them.
And they pray to God that he will not repay those who kill them and flog them, as they drag them
and throw them outside the city,
along with everything they do to them in the synagogues and councils,
and the way they bring them before governors and kings, along with great sufferings, even to the point of death.
So, as we act
